solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relative in America I dressed in fleece

indicators.note: being dressed in something means being wrapped by it, so these letters go inside the swindle word

parts.note: to fleece someone is to con them
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A relative from the States wearing woolly fleece clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of one's aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Writer shielded by scholarly publisher is to speak freely

indicators.note: the writing implement is protected inside the publisher's letters

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author protected by an academic press is free to say what they like.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to talk candidly and without reserve.

clue.text: Trunks match examples

parts.note: to suit is to match or go with
cases are instances or examples

explanation.surface: Swimming trunks that go together with samples.
explanation.definitionFit: Trunks are large travelling cases, as suitcases are luggage.

clue.text: Tend to help married first — I do

indicators.note: the married letter is put before the help word

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone at a wedding saying their vows after promising care.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer speaking: a nursemaid tends to help, so 'I do' says she does the tending.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid's job is to care for children, so the clue's tending is the very thing she claims to do.

clue.text: Fee covering stage performer's training

indicators.note: the fee word wraps around the stage word, covering it on both sides

parts.note: a fee is the price charged
a stage performer's turn is their act

explanation.surface: The cost of lessons for someone learning to perform on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Practice is repeated exercise to gain skill, which is a form of training.

clue.text: Churchman not quite yet out of office?

parts.note: pre- means before, not yet
late means former, no longer holding office

explanation.surface: A clergyman who has not yet quite left his post.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a bishop or other high-ranking member of the clergy.

clue.text: Top Dog's character first seen in Aristophanes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the dominant member of a group, the top dog
second meaning: the Greek letter that begins Aristophanes's name

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha names the leader of a pack and is also the first letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Compact High Street time's forgotten

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters are muddled
forgotten means the time letter is left out of the street word

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A make-up compact bought on the high street, with time slipping by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgotten' drops a T from STREET, leaving SREET, which 'High' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse writing is brief and concise, packing meaning into few words.

clue.text: These should be cold, best outside with sun

indicators.note: the best word sits outside the cold letter

parts.note: choice means the best, top quality
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Ice-cream treats ought to be served chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc-ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate; the whole clue both builds it and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Choc-ices are frozen desserts, so they must be kept chilled.

clue.text: Thoroughbred exercises and I would turn mostly envious

parts.note: PE is physical education, i.e. exercises

indicators.note: turn means the contracted form of I would is read backwards

parts.note: contracted to I'D

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the colour word is dropped

parts.note: green with envy, so green means envious

explanation.surface: A racehorse doing its workouts and a rider who would turn jealous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses I'D to give DI; 'mostly' cuts GREEN to GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree animal has a recorded pure-bred ancestry, as a thoroughbred does; the noun is used here as a label for such stock.

clue.text: Standard scholar's remit

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a don is a university teacher or scholar

explanation.surface: The normal scope of an academic's duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit a punishment or debt is to cancel it, which is what a pardon does to an offence.

clue.text: Courier hiding what's at the heart of this city's might

indicators.note: the courier word conceals the central letters inside itself

parts.note: a mule is a drug courier

indicators.note: the heart of a phrase is its middle letters

parts.note: the central two letters of these words

explanation.surface: A messenger concealing the secret of this city's power.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart is taken across two words, ignoring the space, and the 's is a link meaning 'is'. A mule is a person who smuggles goods, hence courier.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means physical strength or power, as might does.

clue.text: Pedagogue of relevance only in theory

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a teacher or scholar
second meaning: ..., of no practical consequence

explanation.surface: A teacher whose ideas matter only on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word names a university teacher; as an adjective it means theoretical rather than practical.

clue.text: What fundamentally identifies you could be lifted also

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: and means also

explanation.surface: Your basic identity could be stolen as well.
explanation.definitionFit: DNA is the genetic code unique to each person, used to identify them.

clue.text: Uproarious cheer marks an entertainer who mesmerises

indicators.note: uproarious means wild and riotous, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Loud cheering greets a performer who holds the audience spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake charmer is a street performer who appears to hypnotise a snake with a pipe.

clue.text: Breathe in freely and lie up

indicators.note: freely suggests letters released from their order

explanation.surface: Inhale without restriction and rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie up is to rest in a sheltered place, as animals do through winter dormancy.

clue.text: These square up better than granny's bank bonds

definitions.text: These square up better than granny's

parts.note: a reef is a ridge or bank in the sea
knots are ties or bonds

explanation.surface: Bank bonds outperform a grandmother's investments.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny knot is the faulty version of a square knot; the reef knot sits square, the granny doesn't.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot, also called a square knot, lies flat, unlike the slipping granny knot.

clue.text: Time for oats?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a prison sentence, doing time
second meaning: a breakfast dish of oats cooked in milk or water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing porridge' is British slang for serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for a spell in jail and the name of a hot oatmeal breakfast.

clue.text: Loosely describe loan as tidy?

indicators.note: loosely suggests letters set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vague way of saying a loan is neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidy' is used in the sense of a tidy sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a large one, so tidy in that idiom means considerable.

clue.text: One's quiet — unlikely!

parts.note: one is, said in the first person, is I'm
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be silent, which is hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M P spells the answer; and a mischievous imp keeping quiet is unlikely.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a mischievous little sprite or naughty child, rarely a silent one.

clue.text: Sub's reticence to get game going again

definitions.meaning: second meaning: restraint in speech or manner
third meaning: to ... is to serve again, as in tennis

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is'; the third meaning splits as RE-SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a substitute, a shy restraint, and, split, to serve once more to restart play.

clue.text: You'd say a tissue is for this

definitions.text: You'd say a tissue is for this

parts.words: You'd say a tissue is for this
parts.note: a tissue sounds like atishoo, the noise of the reflex, and a tissue is also what you reach for after it

explanation.walkthrough: 'A tissue' spoken aloud is 'atishoo', the noise of the reflex the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is the sudden expulsion of air whose sound is written atishoo, and tissues catch it.

clue.text: For Parisians very flirty play is wrong

parts.note: très is French for very
making a pass is a flirtatious advance

explanation.surface: French people think a very flirtatious move is out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: As nouns, a trespass is an offence or sin, a wrong done to another.

clue.text: Kind about priest — one's a good egg?

indicators.note: the kind word goes about the priest's letter, enclosing it

parts.note: sort means kind or type

explanation.surface: A kindly clergyman is a decent fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport, as in a good sport, is a fair-minded, likeable person.

clue.text: Sadly I can't prank

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone regretfully unable to play a practical joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or absurd trick, a caper or piece of mischief.

clue.text: Family beset by tabloid collecting up scattered stuff

indicators.note: the family word is surrounded by the tabloid word

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
kin are family

explanation.surface: A family hounded by the gutter press gathering up debris.
explanation.definitionFit: Raking is gathering leaves or debris together with a rake.

clue.text: A doctor of sex is deft

parts.note: o' is a shortened of, as in o'clock
it means sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A sex doctor is skilful.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and nimble, the same as deft.

clue.text: Teach about society somebody being well-thought-out

indicators.note: the teaching word goes about the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: to read a lesson or lecture is to teach
one means a person, somebody

explanation.surface: Teaching about society for somebody to become thoughtful.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoned argument has been worked out logically, so it is carefully considered.

clue.text: Camp champ consuming large bit of squid, say

parts.note: a tent is a camping shelter

indicators.note: the champion word eats the size letter, swallowing it

parts.note: an ace is a champion
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A champion at a campsite eating a big piece of calamari.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentacle is one of the long arms of a squid or octopus; 'say' marks squid as one example.

clue.text: Being more comfortable one's dressed in exotic saree

indicators.note: one is clothed by the reworked sari letters, so it goes inside them
exotic means foreign and unusual, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone feels more at ease wearing a foreign sari.
explanation.definitionFit: Easier as a comparative means more relaxed or at ease.
